original_question: (V. V. Uspenskii). A Hausdorff topological group G is called minimal if it does not admit a strictly coarser Hausdorff group topology. A topological group is called Raikov complete if its two-sided uniform structure is complete. It is known that a finite direct product of Raikov complete minimal topological groups is again minimal. Is it true that an arbitrary Cartesian product of Raikov complete minimal topological groups remains minimal? It is known that an arbitrary Cartesian product of centre-free minimal topological groups is minimal(M. Megrelishvili, Topology Appl., 62, no. 1(1995), 1–19).
target_in_paper: Problem 21.103 (V. V. Uspenskii) in the section "New Problems (21st issue, 2026)": whether arbitrary Cartesian products of Raikov complete minimal topological groups must be minimal. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's official problem almost verbatim: it gives the paper's definitions of a minimal Hausdorff topological group and of Raikov completeness, recalls the known finite-product result, asks exactly about arbitrary Cartesian products, and includes the same comparison with Megrelishvili's theorem for centre-free minimal groups. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
missing_details: To make the question fully stand-alone, specify that the Cartesian product carries the usual product topology. This is standard but implicit in the paper's wording. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))

The paper says "an arbitrary Cartesian product," which leaves this quantification implicit. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))

refined_question: Let {G_i}_{i∈I} be an arbitrary family of Hausdorff topological groups, each of which is minimal (that is, it admits no strictly coarser Hausdorff group topology) and Raikov complete (that is, complete with respect to its two-sided uniformity). Must the product topological group ∏_{i∈I} G_i, equipped with the product topology, also be minimal? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
justification: The nearest and exact target is the Kourovka Notebook entry 21.103, not a broader neighboring problem: the entry states precisely this minimality-of-products question, together with the same two definitions and the same two pieces of context used in your draft (finite products are known to stay minimal; arbitrary products are known to be minimal in the centre-free case). The paper does not present an explicit equivalent reformulation of 21.103 nearby, so the sharpest paper-faithful rewrite is simply the fully quantified product-topology version of that same question.
